# Get Reliable DIY Fixes at Home with Perplexity

**A leaky tap, a stuck door, a washing machine error code — Perplexity can give you a focused, sourced answer in seconds.** This guide is for anyone who'd rather fix small things at home than wait three weeks for a tradie, and who wants a smarter way to find trustworthy instructions than scrolling through endless forum threads.

> **A quick honest note:** Perplexity can research and explain. It cannot physically repair anything, and it is not a substitute for a licensed tradesperson when the job involves gas, mains electricity, structural work, or plumbing that requires certification in your state or territory.

## Before you start

- A web browser on your phone or computer (you can use Perplexity without an account, but a free account lets you save your searches).
- Roughly 10 minutes for your first question, including reading the sources.
- A specific home problem in mind — the more detail you can give, the better the answer will be.
- The free plan covers everyday use; the paid "Pro" plan gives you more advanced searches per day and access to stronger AI models.

## Step 1 — Open Perplexity in your browser

Open your browser and go to **perplexity.ai**. The home page shows a single large search bar in the middle with placeholder text like "Ask anything…". You don't need to log in to ask your first questions, but signing in (top-right corner) lets you save your search history for later. If you're on a phone, you can also install the Perplexity app from the App Store or Google Play — it works the same way. The interface is intentionally simple: one search box, a small microphone icon if you'd rather speak your question, and sometimes an attachment icon for uploading a photo of the problem. 💬 Example: just open the page and look at the empty search box — that's all you need to start. You'll know it worked when you see the search bar with the prompt ready for typing.

## Step 2 — Type your home repair question with details

Tap inside the search bar and write your question in plain English. The trick is to include specific details: what the problem is, where it is, and any context that helps. Think of it like describing the issue to a knowledgeable neighbor — the more useful detail you give, the better the answer. Vague questions get vague answers. If your screen looks different, the search bar may sit at the top of the page instead of the middle, or you may need to tap a "New Thread" button first. 💬 Example: "My kitchen tap drips from the spout even when turned off tightly. It's a single-handle mixer tap, about five years old. How do I fix it?" You'll know it worked when you see a loading animation and then a written answer appears with numbered sources listed underneath.

## Step 3 — Read the answer and check the sources

Perplexity writes an answer at the top, then lists the sources it used as small numbered buttons or links just below the text. This is the key difference from a regular AI chatbot — Perplexity shows you where each piece of information came from, so you can verify it. Tap or click each numbered source to open the original webpage in a new tab. Read the answer first, then skim at least two or three sources to confirm the advice matches what a real expert or reputable site is saying. If a source looks unfamiliar or low-quality (a random blog, anonymous forum, content that doesn't name an author), treat that part of the answer with extra caution. 💬 Example: if the answer says "the cartridge inside the tap likely needs replacing," click the source number next to that sentence and read the linked article. You'll know it worked when you've opened at least one source and confirmed the advice matches what an expert would say.

## Step 4 — Ask a follow-up for tools and safety

Now ask a second, narrower question in the same conversation. This is where Perplexity shines — it remembers your first question, so you can build on it. Ask specifically about what tools you'll need, what safety gear to wear, and roughly how long the repair usually takes. If your question involves electricity, gas, water mains, or anything structural, the AI will often warn you to call a licensed tradesperson — pay close attention to that warning. On the free plan, you may notice a daily limit on more advanced searches; basic follow-ups stay free. If your screen looks different, you might need to scroll down to find a "Follow-up" box, or tap a "+" icon to start a new question in the same thread. 💬 Example: "What tools and parts do I need to replace the cartridge in a single-handle kitchen mixer tap? Are there any safety steps I should take first?" You'll know it worked when a fresh answer appears below your first one, with a new list of sources underneath.

## Step 5 — Save or share the answer for later

Once you have what you need, save it so you can refer back when you're standing at the kitchen sink with a wrench in your hand. Look for a "Share" icon (often an arrow or three dots) or a "Copy" button next to the answer. You can copy the whole conversation to your clipboard, share it via email or messages, or — if you're signed in — Perplexity will keep it in your library automatically under a "Threads" or "Library" tab. Print it out if you're heading to the hardware shop, so you can read the tool list in the aisle. If it looks different, the save options might be hidden inside a menu behind three dots in the top-right of the answer. 💬 Example: tap the share icon, choose "Copy link" or "Copy text", then paste it into your phone's notes app with the title "Tap fix — kitchen". You'll know it worked when you can find the saved answer later without searching again.

## Common mistakes

- **Asking too vaguely.** "How do I fix my tap?" gives a thin answer. Add the type of tap, the age, and exactly what it's doing — detail is your friend.
- **Trusting without checking sources.** Perplexity cites real pages, but those pages aren't always authoritative. Always click through at least one or two sources before picking up a tool.
- **Ignoring safety warnings.** The AI is a research helper, not a tradie. For gas, mains electricity, structural repairs, or anything that needs a license in your state or territory, hire a professional.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** small jobs — a dripping tap, a squeaky door hinge, a washing machine error code, a patch of peeling paint — become 20-minute research tasks instead of two-hour forum deep-dives.
- **For your business or work:** if you run a small business from home or manage a rental, quick sourced answers help you decide what's a DIY job and what needs a callout, saving both time and money.
- **If you're just getting started:** pick one small, low-risk repair this weekend — a loose cabinet handle, a blocked showerhead, a smoke alarm battery — and use Perplexity to walk through it before you start.

## Try it now

Open **perplexity.ai** and ask this exact question: "My shower head has low water pressure. I'm renting an apartment, so I can't do major plumbing work. How can I check what's wrong and fix it safely without calling a plumber yet?" Read the answer, click two of the numbered sources, and notice how much faster this is than your usual forum search.
